purpose: Domain vocabulary and business rules. An agent unfamiliar with Indian channel finance should read this before writing scheme or partner logic.

glossary.SC: Scheduled Caste — the beneficiary group this platform serves.
glossary.MoSJE: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment — the sponsoring ministry.
glossary.NSFDC: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation — apex body whose concessional credit products this app surfaces.
glossary.Channel Finance System: The routing model: beneficiaries cannot apply to NSFDC directly. Funds flow through 100+ Channel Partners.
glossary.Channel Partner: An authorised intermediary that receives and processes loan applications. Four types: SCA, PSB, RRB, NBFC-MFI.
glossary.SCA: State Channelizing Agency — the state-level corporation, usually the widest scheme coverage.
glossary.PSB: Public Sector Bank — typically handles larger term loans and education loans.
glossary.RRB: Regional Rural Bank — rural reach, agriculture and micro-credit.
glossary.NBFC-MFI: Non-Banking Financial Company / Micro Finance Institution — small-ticket micro-credit.
glossary.NPA: Non-Performing Asset — a loan in default. A partner with high NPAs is a bad routing target because disbursement stalls.
glossary.Moratorium: Repayment holiday after disbursement (3–12 months here) before the first EMI falls due. Interest still accrues.
glossary.Margin money: The beneficiary's own contribution — project cost minus the sanctioned loan.
glossary.Funding share: Proportion of project cost the scheme funds. 90% is standard for these products.
glossary.Concessional rate: Below-market interest rate, the core benefit of these schemes.

coreRules.rule: Annual family income must not exceed ₹5,00,000.
coreRules.effect: Hard eligibility gate. Fails → no scheme is recommended, with the reason shown.

coreRules.rule: Schemes fund up to 90% of project cost, capped by the scheme's own ceiling.
Ticket size selects the product family: Micro Finance up to a ₹1.40 lakh unit cost (max loan ₹1.25 lakh), Term Loan above ₹1.25 lakh up to a ₹50 lakh project (max loan ₹45 lakh).
coreRules.effect: Drives which schemes score highest for a given project cost. Verified against nsfdc.nic.in/scheme on 2026-09-07.

coreRules.rule: Education loans are only for education; business loans are only for business.
coreRules.effect: Hard gate both ways — an applicant asking about course fees must not be shown a term loan and vice versa.

coreRules.rule: Several schemes reserve eligibility for women, and several offer women a lower rate.
coreRules.effect: womenInterestRatePct is preferred when the applicant is female.

coreRules.rule: Never route to a Channel Partner that cannot disburse. NSFDC's conditions are partner-type-specific and must not be flattened into one threshold — see partnerEligibilityNorms.
coreRules.effect: PartnerSearchRequest.onlyAccepting defaults to true. No norm can currently be evaluated, because NSFDC publishes the rules and not the per-partner figures, so every partner is UNKNOWN and is still shown — we cannot assert unavailability either. The UI lists the norms for that partner type and names the missing data.
coreRules.codeLocation: src/features/partners/eligibilityNorms.ts (the norms); src/components/domain/PartnerNorms.tsx (the UI); src/api/mock/server.ts (mockSearchPartners); the real assessment belongs on the server
coreRules.verified: Corrected 2026-09-07. The previous text said 'net NPA below 10% ... or a 5-year average below 10%' as if it were the general rule. That is the Stand-up India condition for RRBs. The general allocation norm for an RRB is net NPA below 15% in at least 3 of the last 6 years. An NBFC-MFI must be below 0.5%. One threshold was wrong for every partner type.

coreRules.rule: Not every partner type processes every scheme category.
coreRules.effect: Scheme.channelPartnerTypes and ChannelPartner.supportedSchemeCategories must both be respected when routing.

schemeCategories.MICRO_FINANCE: Small ticket, petty trade and vending. Typically up to ₹1.40 lakh.
schemeCategories.TERM_LOAN: Larger self-employment projects. Up to ₹50 lakh.
schemeCategories.EDUCATION_LOAN: Professional/technical course fees, India or abroad.
schemeCategories.WOMEN_SPECIFIC: Reserved for women beneficiaries, lowest concessional rates.
schemeCategories.GREEN_MOBILITY: Clean-energy livelihood assets such as e-rickshaws and solar units.

dataVerificationStatus.noWomensRate: No women-specific concessional interest rate could be found on any official page. The earlier seed data invented one; it has been removed. Mahila Samriddhi Yojana is genuinely women-only, which is a separate thing from a discounted rate.

partnerDataStatus.notAvailable: Per-partner NPA, profit history, overdue and utilisation figures are not published anywhere public. Requirement R3 cannot be fully satisfied from open data — it needs a feed from NSFDC. Every partner is therefore status UNKNOWN. requiredInputsFor() in src/features/partners/eligibilityNorms.ts derives the exact field list per partner type; that list is the ask for NSFDC.
partnerDataStatus.removed: The entire v0 seed directory. It invented agencies that do not exist (there is no 'Maharashtra SC Finance & Development Corporation'), two fictional NBFC-MFIs, ten fabricated phone numbers, and NPA percentages attributed to named organisations — the last being a defamatory claim about real institutions, and a fake phone number in a Call button dials a real stranger.

partnerEligibilityNorms.provenance: NSFDC restructured its site: nsfdc.nic.in/scheme serves 200, but every /en/* path now returns 404 — including allocation-of-funds, stand-up-india and the NBFC-MFI criteria page. Every norm was then read VERBATIM from a Wayback Machine capture of the original NSFDC page (allocation-of-funds 2025-03-17, stand-up-india 2024-10-04, NBFC-MFI 2025-02-15). Those are primary documents at permanent URLs, so these are real citations, held at confidence 0.9 rather than 1 only because the captures are 1-2 years old and the live pages are gone, so a later revision would be invisible to us.
common: No amount overdue to NSFDC older than one year at the end of the preceding financial year.
At least 80% cumulative utilisation of funds already disbursed (measured at the end of the preceding month up to February; at the end of the preceding day during March).

SCA: Adequate State Government or bank guarantee in place.
RRB: Net NPA below 15% in at least 3 of the last 6 years preceding disbursement.
Net profit in at least 3 of the last 6 financial years.

Under Stand-up India only, a tighter test: net NPA below 10% for the preceding financial year, or a 5-year average below 10% with net NPA below 10% in at least 3 individual years; profit in the last financial year or in at least 3 of the last 5; not a defaulter of any regulatory body.
PSB: A Memorandum of Agreement with NSFDC in force.
A utilisation certificate filed for the interest-rate switchover from Bank rate to NSFDC rate on earlier refinance.
No overdues payable to NSFDC at the time of disbursement.
NBFC_MFI: Registered with the RBI as an NBFC-MFI and following RBI micro-finance norms.
Gross NPA below 2% and net NPA below 0.5% per the preceding financial year's annual accounts.
Minimum capacity assessment rating of mfr5 (CRISIL or equivalent).
No default on outside borrowings in the last three years and no corporate debt restructuring.

partnerEligibilityNorms.whyThisMatters: The spread is the point: an RRB may carry a net NPA up to 15% and stay eligible while an NBFC-MFI must stay below 0.5% — a thirtyfold difference inside the same network. Any single 'NPA below X%' rule is wrong for at least three of the four partner types.

allocationTargetsNotEligibility.warning: These are targets NSFDC sets for how SCAs should distribute their lending. They are NOT applicant eligibility criteria and must not be turned into a recommender score — being a woman does not make a scheme more suitable, it makes the SCA more motivated. Recorded for pitch context and for a future partner-level view only.
allocationTargetsNotEligibility.security: SCAs provide a Government or Bank Guarantee to NSFDC, preferably as a block guarantee.
allocationTargetsNotEligibility.source: NSFDC — Allocation of Funds, 2025-03-17 archive capture
